arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which ḥadīth of the Arbaʿīn is called <bdi>أُمّ الحَدِيث</bdi>?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Ḥadīth 2 — Ḥadīth Jibrīl

arbaeen_ahadith.front: <bdi>أُمّ الحَدِيث</bdi> is named on the model of which other title?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: <bdi>أُمّ القُرْآن</bdi> — al-Fātiḥah

arbaeen_ahadith.front: According to Ibn Ḥajar, when in the Prophet's ﷺ life did the event of Ḥadīth Jibrīl take place?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Near the end of his life

arbaeen_ahadith.text: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, the man seemed a traveller because {{c1::no one present knew him}}, yet {{c2::his clothes were clean and he bore no marks of travel}}

In Ḥadīth Jibrīl the four questions are about {{c1::<bdi>الإِسْلَام</bdi> (Islām)}}, {{c2::<bdi>الإِيمَان</bdi> (Īmān)}}, {{c3::<bdi>الإِحْسَان</bdi> (Iḥsān)}}, and {{c4::<bdi>السَّاعَة</bdi> (the Hour)}}
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: In the order they are asked.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, how does the Prophet ﷺ answer “What is Islām?”
arbaeen_ahadith.back: With the five pillars

arbaeen_ahadith.text: <bdi>إِسْلَام</bdi>, <bdi>إِيمَان</bdi> and <bdi>إِحْسَان</bdi> are the <bdi>مَصَادِر</bdi> of {{c1::<bdi>أَسْلَمَ</bdi>}}, {{c2::<bdi>آمَنَ</bdi>}} and {{c3::<bdi>أَحْسَنَ</bdi>}} — all Form {{c4::IV}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does <bdi>إِسْلَام</bdi> mean linguistically?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Obedience, servitude

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Technically, <bdi>الإِسْلَام</bdi> has two definitions: {{c1::the proper name of the entire way of life revealed by Allah}}, and {{c2::external submission — <bdi>الاِنْقِيَادُ الظَّاهِرِيُّ</bdi>}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why did the Prophet ﷺ define Islām by the five pillars?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Because Islām, technically, is external submission — <bdi>الاِنْقِيَادُ الظَّاهِرِيُّ</bdi>

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In defining Islām by five pillars, what did the Prophet ﷺ intend the five to stand for?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Five categories of submission — not a limit on what Islām is

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The five pillars as categories of submission: shahādah — {{c1::verbal}}; prayer — {{c2::physical}}; fasting — {{c3::refraining}}; zakāh — {{c4::financial}}; ḥajj — {{c5::all of them together}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, the Prophet's ﷺ answer about īmān is not a definition — what does it do instead?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It describes what one must believe in — the six pillars of faith

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The six pillars of faith in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: belief in {{c1::Allah}}, {{c2::His angels}}, {{c3::His books}}, {{c4::His messengers}}, {{c5::the Last Day}}, and {{c6::<bdi>القَدَر</bdi> (qadar)}}

{{c1::Tawḥīd}} is the cornerstone of ʿaqīdah. Its three components: Allah is without partner in His {{c2::dominion}}; without likeness in His {{c3::essence (<bdi>ذَات</bdi>) and attributes (<bdi>صِفَات</bdi>)}}; and alone {{c4::deserving of worship}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does belief in the angels comprise?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Belief in their existence, their tasks and their descriptions — though we cannot see them

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Besides the books themselves, what does belief in the books of Allah include?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That the last and final book is the Qurʾān

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does belief in the messengers require?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Accepting every messenger and prophet Allah sent to guide humanity, including the final messenger Muḥammad ﷺ

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Belief in the Last Day: that there is {{c1::life after death}}, with {{c2::accountability before Allah}}; that it {{c3::lasts for eternity}}; and that {{c4::we will be resurrected}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which of the six pillars of faith is the most complex and difficult to understand?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> (qadar) — divine decree

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> covers which kinds of decree?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Both the good and the bad

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Belief in <bdi>القَدَر</bdi> includes belief in Allah's {{c1::pre-eternal knowledge}} and in {{c2::<bdi>اللَّوْح المَحْفُوظ</bdi> (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ)}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is belief in <bdi>القَضَاء</bdi> (al-qaḍāʾ)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Understanding that nothing happens without the will and decree of Allah

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What must belief in qadar be balanced against?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That we still have a level of free will, and are accountable for our own choices

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What analogy shows Allah's foreknowledge without removing a person's responsibility?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A teacher knows which students are putting in effort, so knows who will fail the final — yet the student can blame no one but themselves

arbaeen_ahadith.text: <bdi>أَمِنَ يَأْمَنُ</bdi> means {{c1::to feel safe}}; its Form IV <bdi>آمَنَ</bdi> means {{c2::to make someone feel safe}}, and later came to convey {{c3::<bdi>تَصْدِيق</bdi> (taṣdīq) — affirming, believing}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why do scholars' technical definitions of īmān differ?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Each defined it within their own theological context

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which two schools did the scholars of Kalām mostly belong to?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The Ashʿarīs and the Māturīdīs

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What were the scholars of Kalām often doing, and in whose language?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Refuting philosophy — using the language of Greek logic

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How did the scholars of Kalām define īmān?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Affirming everything necessarily known to have come from the religion of the Prophet ﷺ

arbaeen_ahadith.text: {{c1::التَّصْدِيقُ}} بِمَا عُلِمَ مَجِيئُهُ {{c2::ضَرُورَةً}} مِنْ دِينِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ

arbaeen_ahadith.front: On the Kalām definition, what kind of act is īmān?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: An action of the heart alone

arbaeen_ahadith.front: On the Kalām definition of īmān, what is kufr?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Its opposite — not affirming what is necessarily known to be from the Prophet's ﷺ religion

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The Atharīs defined īmān as belief {{c1::in the heart}}, declaration {{c2::with the tongue}}, and action {{c3::with the limbs}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which group was the Atharī definition of īmān a response to?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The Murjiʾah — <bdi>المُرْجِئَة</bdi>

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What did the Murjiʾah hold about īmān?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That only the actions of the heart are required

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Complete the Prophet's ﷺ answer about iḥsān: “To worship Allah as if …”
arbaeen_ahadith.back: …you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He truly sees you

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does <bdi>إِحْسَان</bdi> mean linguistically?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Perfection, goodness

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is iḥsān, technically?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Doing things in the best way possible

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is iḥsān said to be the hallmark of?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: An upright, moral, God-conscious believer

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Of islām, īmān and iḥsān, which is the highest stage?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Iḥsān

arbaeen_ahadith.text: The scholars of Taṣawwuf see two stages of iḥsān in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: {{c1::worshipping as if you see Allah}} — reached only in the hereafter — and {{c2::knowing that He sees you}}, the stage through which iḥsān is achieved now
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: The second stage is reconstructed from the ḥadīth. Your notes name only the first.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In Ḥadīth Jibrīl, what did the Prophet ﷺ reply when asked when the Hour will come?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That he knew no more about it than the one asking

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Whose knowledge alone is the timing of the Hour?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Allah's alone

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Complete the sign of the Hour in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: “The slave woman will give birth to …”
arbaeen_ahadith.back: …her own owner

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Complete the sign of the Hour in Ḥadīth Jibrīl: “The barefoot, destitute, unclothed shepherds …”
arbaeen_ahadith.back: …will compete in building tall buildings

arbaeen_ahadith.text: “The slave woman will give birth to her owner” is read as {{c1::widespread ignorance of Islamic law}}, or figuratively as {{c2::children treating their mothers like slaves}}
“The shepherds will compete in building tall buildings” is read literally — {{c1::something we see today}} — or figuratively, as {{c2::the affairs of the world turned upside down}}

wrel.front: Who founded Confucianism, and roughly when and where?
wrel.back: Confucius — around 500 BCE, in China

wrel.front: On the lecture's account, what role did Confucianism play across East Asian societies?
wrel.back: The foundation of their development — the ethical construct that guided them

wrel.front: What is Confucianism's central focus?
wrel.back: Ethics — what it means to be a good person

wrel.front: What attitude to the past does Confucianism hold?
wrel.back: Veneration of it

wrel.front: How does Confucianism relate individual conduct to society?
wrel.back: Conduct is tied to the social order: no one exists as an individual apart from society, so the question is how to be good in relation to it

wrel.meaning: children respecting their parents, caring for them, and making sure they are at ease — a core Confucian value

wrel.front: What happened when other religions mixed with Confucianism?
wrel.back: They became new religions of their own, or a part of Confucianism

wrel.front: To whom is Daoism attributed, and roughly when and where?
wrel.back: Laozi — 6th century BCE, in China

wrel.meaning: “old master” — the figure Daoism is attributed to

wrel.front: What is uncertain about Laozi?
wrel.back: Whether he was a real person

wrel.front: What stance toward worldly affairs does Daoism teach?
wrel.back: Passive withdrawal from them

wrel.front: Instead of ambition, what does Daoism tell a person to do?
wrel.back: Observe nature and copy how it acts — flowing, not rushing — staying in tune with it

wrel.front: What quest is Daoism often associated with?
wrel.back: Long life, immortality, and overcoming physical limitations

wrel.front: According to the lecture, where did many Daoist practices come from?
wrel.back: Buddhism

wrel.front: What is Shinto?
wrel.back: The indigenous religion of Japan

wrel.text: Shinto has no {{c1::founder}}, no {{c2::founding date}}, and no {{c3::major sacred text}}

wrel.meaning: in Shinto, a spiritual, life-giving force that may inhabit natural phenomena

wrel.front: What practical attitude follows from belief in kami?
wrel.back: Not harming or annoying the spirits

wrel.front: Who founded Buddhism, and roughly when?
wrel.back: Siddhārtha Gautama — the 6th or 5th century BCE

wrel.front: What status did Buddhism hold in many East Asian countries?
wrel.back: State religion

wrel.text: Buddhism has a concept of {{c1::heaven and hell}}, of {{c2::saints to worship}}, and of beings {{c3::somewhat like angels}}

wrel.front: How many buddhas are there, and which one does the course mean by “the Buddha”?
wrel.back: More than one — the course means the historical Buddha

wrel.front: What is paradoxical about the historical Buddha's status in Buddhism?
wrel.back: He is not considered a god, yet he is one of the objects of worship

wrel.front: What institutional system does Buddhism have?
wrel.back: Monasticism

wrel.front: What do the salvation-oriented Buddhist sects hold?
wrel.back: That the world is so corrupt the only way to be saved is for the Buddha to take you to paradise

wrel.front: What idea is Buddhism said to have introduced?
wrel.back: Funerary rites

wrel.front: Which of the major East Asian traditions does the lecture call inclusive rather than exclusive?
wrel.back: All four — Confucianism, Daoism, Shinto, and Buddhism

wrel.front: Where does the word now widely used for “religion” in East Asia come from?
wrel.back: A Japanese translation of the European concept

wrel.front: What words were used before it for what we call religion, and still are?
wrel.back: “Teaching”, “school of”, “way”, “path”

wrel.text: East Asian folk religions have no {{c1::founder}}, no {{c2::founding date}}, and no {{c3::doxa}}

wrel.front: What follows from folk religions developing organically, without a clear start?
wrel.back: There is no clear division between one religious practice and another

wrel.front: What do folk religions tend to focus on?
wrel.back: The calendar, ritual cycles, and belief in spirits

wrel.front: For whom are folk religions often a form of religious expression?
wrel.back: Women — female shamanesses, for example

wrel.front: How do folk religions relate to the major traditions?
wrel.back: They accommodate and fuse with them

quduri.front: What is the primary means of achieving ritual purity?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: Which two questions does the section on water answer?
quduri.back: Which water can be used for wuḍūʾ and ghusl, and which can remove impurity
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: Why is the classification of water less pressing today?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: The fuqahāʾ divide water into three: {{c1::<bdi>طَهُور</bdi> (ṭahūr)::pure and purifying}}, {{c2::<bdi>طَاهِر</bdi> (ṭāhir)::pure, not purifying}}, and {{c3::<bdi>نَجِس</bdi> (najis)::impure}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.back: Whether it purifies — both are pure in themselves, but only <bdi>طَهُور</bdi> is <bdi>مُطَهِّر</bdi>
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.meaning: water already used for wuḍūʾ or ghusl, and collected
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: Which of the three types of water is <bdi>مَاء مُسْتَعْمَل</bdi>?
quduri.back: <bdi>طَاهِر</bdi> — not impure, but it cannot be used for ṭahārah
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.meaning: unqualified water — water called simply “water”, as against qualified water such as rose water
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: What is the ruling on <bdi>مَاء مُطْلَق</bdi>?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: With which kind of water does al-Qudūrī open the discussion?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: The <bdi>مَاء مُطْلَق</bdi> al-Qudūrī lists: {{c1::water from the sky — rain, snow}}; {{c2::rivers}}; {{c3::springs}}; {{c4::wells}}; {{c5::the sea}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: When does water stop counting as water?
quduri.back: When something else dominates it and takes it out of its nature (<bdi>طَبْع</bdi>)
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: <bdi>طَبْع المَاء</bdi>, the nature of water, is its {{c1::<bdi>رِقَّة</bdi>}} (thinness) and its {{c2::<bdi>سَيَلَان</bdi>}} (flowing)
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: <bdi>أَوْصَاف المَاء</bdi>, the qualities of water, are its {{c1::<bdi>طَعْم</bdi>}} (taste), {{c2::<bdi>لَوْن</bdi>}} (colour) and {{c3::<bdi>رِيح</bdi>}} (smell)
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.meaning: mixed water — water with another substance in it
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: Mixed water: if the substance is {{c1::pure (<bdi>طَاهِر</bdi>)}}, it turns on whether it is {{c2::solid or liquid}}; if it is {{c3::impure (<bdi>نَجِس</bdi>)}}, on whether the water is {{c4::flowing or standing}}, then on {{c5::its quantity}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.text: Water mixed with a pure solid (<bdi>جَامِد</bdi>) is judged by its {{c1::<bdi>طَبْع</bdi> — thinness and flowing}}; with a pure liquid (<bdi>مَائِع</bdi>), by its {{c2::<bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> — taste, colour and smell}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: How much may water mixed with a pure liquid change and remain usable?
quduri.back: At least two of its three <bdi>أَوْصَاف</bdi> must remain — one may change, not more
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: What is the ruling on flowing water (<bdi>جَارٍ</bdi>) into which najāsah falls?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: What is the ruling on a small quantity (<bdi>قَلِيل</bdi>) of standing water (<bdi>رَاكِد</bdi>) into which najāsah falls?
quduri.back: Unusable — even a single drop makes it najis
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: What is the ruling on a large quantity (<bdi>كَثِير</bdi>) of standing water into which najāsah falls?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

quduri.front: For the Aḥnāf, what counts as a large quantity of standing water?
quduri.back: 10 × 10 arm-lengths (<bdi>ذِرَاع</bdi>) in area, deep enough that scooping water does not expose the ground
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah, water, class notes 2026-09-30

riyad.front: What is the ruling on repentance (<bdi>تَوْبَة</bdi>)?
riyad.source: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes
Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes

riyad.text: The conditions of <bdi>تَوْبَة</bdi> for a sin between a person and Allah: {{c1::stopping the sin}}; {{c2::feeling regret}}; {{c3::resolving not to return to it}}
riyad.source: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes

riyad.front: What happens to <bdi>تَوْبَة</bdi> if one of its conditions is missing?
riyad.source: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes

riyad.front: What further condition does <bdi>تَوْبَة</bdi> carry when the sin involves another person's right?
riyad.back: Restoring that right to them — returning wealth, for example
riyad.source: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes

riyad.front: When the sin involves a <bdi>حَدّ</bdi> (ḥadd) owed to someone, how is their right restored?
riyad.back: By allowing the ḥadd to be carried out, or by seeking their pardon
riyad.source: Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn — Chapter of Repentance, class notes
